title: Do most Africans live in villages?
subtitle: About 45 in every 100 Africans lived in a town or city in 2023, and in 23 of the 54 countries most people did.

parts.text: The picture of Africa as a continent of villages is old and sticks. Village life is real for very many people. It is not the whole picture.
In 2023 about 672 million people in the 54 countries lived in urban areas, out of about 1,478 million.
That is about 45%, calculated here by adding the countries' figures.
In 23 of the 54 countries, more than half the people were urban.
Counted this way, the other 31 were mostly rural.
The urban share runs from about 17% in Malawi to about 92% in Gabon.
Niger, South Sudan and Ethiopia are below 25%; Libya is at 88%.
So "most Africans live in villages" is true of some countries and false of others, and the share moves with every year.

gaps: The figures follow each country's own definition of urban, which differs from country to country; we have not compared those definitions here.
The sums and percentages are our own arithmetic on 2023 World Bank values. The 2025 population on the Countries page is a different year.
The data say how many people live in places counted as urban, not how those places look or what work people do there.
